core_obligations: Replace the target by the open image of the morphism, using that etale morphisms are open, so that the morphism may be assumed surjective (proof lines 6626-6629).
Observe that the morphism is then bijective and open, hence a homeomorphism, and in particular quasi-compact (proof lines 6630-6631).
Invoke the criterion that a flat, surjective and quasi-compact monomorphism is an isomorphism, reducing the assertion to showing that the morphism is a monomorphism (proof lines 6631-6633).

Show that the diagonal is an open immersion because the morphism is etale, that it is surjective because the morphism is universally injective, and hence that it is an isomorphism, which is precisely the statement that the morphism is a monomorphism (proof lines 6633-6640).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the surjective case by taking the image (proof lines 6626-6629).
A bijective open map is a homeomorphism, hence quasi-compact (proof lines 6630-6631).
Reduce to being a monomorphism, by the flat surjective quasi-compact criterion (proof lines 6631-6633).
The diagonal is an open immersion and surjective, hence an isomorphism (proof lines 6633-6640).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a single sentence -- a universally injective etale morphism of schemes is an open immersion -- and its first proof is a sequence of carefully chosen reductions (statement lines 6620-6623, proof lines 6625-6641). The morphism is first replaced by its image, which is open because etale morphisms are open, so that one may assume it surjective; it is then bijective and open, hence a homeomorphism, and in particular quasi-compact. At that point the author invokes the criterion that a flat, surjective, quasi-compact monomorphism is an isomorphism, so the task becomes showing that the morphism is a monomorphism, which is done by observing that for an etale morphism the diagonal is an open immersion, that universal injectivity makes the diagonal surjective, and that an open immersion which is surjective is an isomorphism. The claim is H2: there is one line of argument rather than several independent ones, but it consists of a reduction to the surjective case, an application of a criterion, and an identification of the diagonal, each of which has to be seen.
